props.title: Vanity Fair
props.initialSlug: A world of envy, greed, and ambition.

sections.content: Vanity Fair stands as a vibrant adaptation of William Makepeace Thackeray's satirical masterpiece, with Mira Nair bringing her distinct visual flair to Victorian England. Like Joe Wright's Pride & Prejudice (2005) and Ang Lee's Sense and Sensibility (1995), it transforms classic literature into sumptuous cinema. Reese Witherspoon's Becky Sharp blazes through society with calculated charm, while the film's rich production design and Gabriel Yared's score create an intoxicating period atmosphere that rivals The Age of Innocence (1993).

sections.content: Nair's direction infuses the traditional period piece with exotic flourishes and Indian influences, reflecting both the reach of the British Empire and her own cinematic heritage. This multicultural approach anticipates later genre innovations like Belle (2013) and The Personal History of David Copperfield (2019), which challenge the typical whitewashed view of Victorian England. The film's lavish costume design by Beatrix Aruna Pasztor deserves particular attention, using color and detail to track Becky's social climbing.

While some critics found Witherspoon's modern energy jarring, her performance connects to a tradition of bold literary heroines in film, from Jennifer Jones in Madame Bovary (1949) to Keira Knightley in Anna Karenina (2012). The film's exploration of ambition and gender politics remains startlingly relevant, particularly in scenes showing how Becky must navigate male-dominated spaces with wit as her only weapon. sections.content: Vanity Fair breaks from traditional period drama constraints in ways that influenced later adaptations. Like Sofia Coppola's Marie Antoinette (2006), it employs contemporary storytelling techniques and modern music cues to make historical material feel immediate and vital. The film's critical view of colonialism and class mobility anticipates works like The Favourite (2018) and Bridgerton (2020), which similarly deconstruct period piece conventions.
